section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single study (Study X) of 309 Portuguese women examining how social safeness relates to eating psychopathology via self-reassurance and body appreciation; the authors report that self-reassurance and body appreciation mediate much of the protective effect of social safeness on restraint and concerns (models explaining 22–51% depending on outcome). The section notes limitations including cross-sectional design, exclusive use of self-report measures, and a women-only Portuguese community sample, and suggests future research should include males, clinical samples, and longitudinal or multi-group BMI analyses.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The present study, conducted in a sample of 309 Portuguese women, thus aimed to test an innovative model..."; "the association between social safeness and body appreciation is mediated by the mechanisms of self-reassurance."; "in a model that explained 22, 27, 51, and 47% of restraint, eating concern, weight concern, and shape concern, respectively."; "the selection of a sample exclusively composed of women from the Portuguese general population prevents the generalization of the results."

section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses results from a single study (Study X) of 309 Portuguese women examining links among social safeness, self-reassurance, body appreciation, and eating psychopathology, with BMI controlled. It reports that self-reassurance mediates the relationship between social safeness and body appreciation and that this pathway helps explain lower levels of disordered eating symptoms.
